newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czechs fighter decision not seen soon - minister.
newsitem.headline: Czechs fighter decision not seen soon - minister.

text.p: The choice of supersonic fighter aircraft to update the Czech Army's fleet of Soviet-made MiGs, is not expected soon, Defence Minister Miloslav Vyborny said on Monday.

"I don't expect that the government now or in the short term would say 'We want to equip with this or that type of supersonic aircraft'," Vyborny said in a live interview on the independent Czech radio station Frequency 1.
"It would neither be an effective nor economic approach... We must create a clear process of selection of a supplier and the criteria for selecting the most advantageous aeroplane," Vyborny added.
Defence contractors from the United States, Britain, Sweden, France, and other countries have been heavily lobbying the Czech government, as it considers how to update the army's fleet.
Czech officials have said they would need about 24 fighters to replace their ageing Soviet made MiG-21s to be more compatible with NATO, but they have said new western planes are too pricey.

Czech officials have said they have the will but not the wallet to buy brand new Western-made advanced fighters, but are keeping their options open as a battle over the long-term military budget goes on.
